question: Which supplied exact identities are false, which named implementations have a measured finite advantage, and which proposed closures remain unsupported after matched controls?
decision_value: Verified counterexamples immediately correct literal identities; passing controls plus held-out measurements decide whether a named algorithm warrants a focused follow-up; bounded nulls delimit only their declared family, while proof-kind closure remains gated on an exact theorem or checked proof.
